Types of Manifold Valves: Quick Selection Table

Types of manifold valves are grouped by how many valves sit inside one block: the 2-valve, 3-valve and 5-valve manifold. Each valve inside the block also has its own job, such as block (isolation), bleed, equalizing or vent. The table below puts the three types side by side so you can pick the right one for a gauge, a pressure transmitter or a DP transmitter.

Manifold typeValves inside the blockNormal operationTypical instrument
2-valve1 block valve, 1 bleed or test valveBlock open, bleed closedPressure gauge, pressure transmitter, pressure switch
3-valve2 block valves, 1 equalizing valveBoth blocks open, equalizer closedDP transmitter for flow or level
5-valve2 block valves, 1 equalizing valve, 2 vent or test valvesBlocks open, equalizer and vents closedDP transmitter where venting and in situ calibration are needed

How to Choose Between the Types

  1. Count the process connections. One connection means a 2-valve manifold, because the 3-valve and 5-valve types need a high side and a low side.
  2. For DP service, decide if you need vent or test ports. Without them a 3-valve manifold is enough for zero checks.
  3. Choose the 5-valve type when technicians must vent pressure and connect a calibrator without removing the transmitter.
  4. Pick a horizontal or vertical body and a direct or remote mounting style to suit the space and process temperature.

Whatever the type, never open the equalizing valve while both block valves are open, or process fluid will pass from the high pressure side to the low pressure side.
